title: Physics on arXiv — 22 October 2026 (notable recent papers)
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart. This is an inferred ranking based on paper-specific scientific signals, not readership or downloads; citation evidence is limited for papers only hours old.

sections.title: PSR J0653+0443: An Eclipsing Millisecond Pulsar in an Extremely Eccentric Double Neutron Star System
sections.abstract: FAST discovery of an extremely eccentric double-neutron-star binary with eccentricity 0.992387, an 85-second eclipse, and unusual pulse timing near periastron.
sections.claimed_result: From more than two years of FAST timing, the authors infer a nearly edge-on DNS system and constrain its non-relativistic periastron advance; population synthesis makes such systems rare.
sections.evidence_type: observational; FAST radio observations and phase-connected pulse-timing analysis
sections.unique_caveat: Formation history and rarity depend on binary-evolution and population-synthesis assumptions; one system is not a population measurement.

sections.title: Meter-scale quantum interconnects between large quantum processors
sections.abstract: Four superconducting-cable links connect two 120-qubit processors, with state transfer, remote CZ gates, and entanglement across modules.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 99.00% mean state-transfer fidelity and 94.75% mean fidelity for distant CZ gates, with entangled states across processors.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; two IBM Nighthawk R1 processors and four 80-cm aluminum coaxial L-couplers
sections.unique_caveat: Only two modules and four links were demonstrated; link loss and cooldown reproducibility remain scale-up concerns.

sections.title: International atomic clock comparison achieving 5×10^-18 uncertainty
sections.abstract: Two independently developed ytterbium-ion optical clocks in the UK and Germany agree to a fractional frequency difference of 1.0(4.8)×10^-18 over a 2,220-km fiber link.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find no statistically significant Lorentz-violating modulation and improve the uncertainty on a Robertson–Mansouri–Sexl parameter constraint by about a factor of five.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; two single-ion 171Yb+ E3 clocks linked by a phase-stabilized 2,220-km optical fiber network
sections.unique_caveat: Relativistic redshift correction including time-varying gravity potential dominates uncertainty; this is not a redefinition of the SI second.

sections.title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). A systematic study of the intracluster light fraction at 0.2 < z < 1.5
sections.abstract: Across roughly 300 clusters, the authors estimate ICL at about 40% of BCG-plus-ICL light and 20% of total cluster stellar light, approximately stable at fixed mass over 0.2<z<1.5.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer that the relative BCG/ICL/satellite partition is largely established by z~1.5, while noting the sample is not an evolutionary sequence.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Euclid Q1 imaging and SPT/optically selected cluster samples, compared with Hydrangea simulations
sections.unique_caveat: ICL fraction depends on wavelength and measurement choices; the sample cannot track evolution of individual clusters.

sections.title: NGC 3227 Blinks: An Extreme Changing-Look Event in a Seyfert Galaxy
sections.abstract: NGC 3227 faded by over 70% in optical continuum and nearly lost broad H-beta within weeks, then recovered within two months, with X-ray hardening and persistent reverberation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors argue a compact Compton-thick obscurer inside the broad-line region explains the fast optical suppression while reverberation continues.
sections.evidence_type: observational; optical monitoring, Swift X-ray observations, reverberation mapping, and supporting variability/photoionization analyses
sections.unique_caveat: The obscurer interpretation is model-dependent, and one event does not establish prevalence.

sections.title: Cosmic Ray Observations using Coincident Scintillator and Radio Signals with BEACON
sections.abstract: BEACON reports 22 candidate cosmic-ray events selected from coincident scintillator and radio data, with polarization consistent with geomagnetic emission.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report candidate cosmic-ray detections and find that simulated hybrid-instrument performance reproduces the observed rate to within an order of magnitude; this is not tau-neutrino detection.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; BEACON six-antenna radio prototype and scintillator-coincidence dataset, with detector simulations
sections.unique_caveat: Events are candidates and the quoted background comes from synthetic pairings; more exposure and independent reconstruction are needed.

sections.title: Spatial Control of Compressible Active Fluids
sections.abstract: Experiments and continuum theory show that patterned activity redistributes microtubules in an active fluid, with density contrast depending on wavelength and vortex structure.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that nematic active stress plus isotropic active pressure reproduce observed modulation and explain suppression at short wavelengths.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; patterned-activity microtubule active-fluid experiments and continuum modeling
sections.unique_caveat: Results are tied to the tested microtubule system and sinusoidal activity patterns; generality to other active materials remains untested.

sections.title: Pure dephasing destroys two-photon amplitude, not nonlinear phase
sections.abstract: For a chiral waveguide-emitter model, a closed-form dephased two-photon scattering calculation leaves the conditional phase at π while suppressing the amplitude carrying it.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find unequal attenuation of one- and two-photon channels and that standard correlator factorization misses 16–81% of pairs over the modeled dephasing range.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; two-photon scattering calculation cross-checked with a Fock-state master equation
sections.unique_caveat: Model-based prediction, not a hardware measurement; implications depend on emitter-waveguide assumptions and dephasing regime.
